pages.headline: Water for Injection by distillation
pages.lead: Our multi-effect and vapour compression stills turn Purified Water into hot Water for Injection (WFI) with endotoxins below 0.25 EU/mL, the method with the longest inspection history in North America and Europe.

blocks.caption: WFI by distillation · USP and Ph. Eur.

Plant steam boils feed water in the first column. The pure vapour from each column heats the next one, so one kilogram of plant steam produces several kilograms of WFI. Droplets and endotoxins are separated before the vapour condenses. Concentrate leaves to drain from the last column.

body: A multi-effect still uses plant steam and reuses its energy across several columns. More effects mean less steam per litre but a higher purchase cost. It needs cooling water at the final condenser and suits sites with spare plant steam.

A vapour compression still uses an electric compressor to raise the pressure of its own vapour, then condenses it to heat incoming feed. It needs little or no cooling water and plant steam only for start-up, and it can accept softened, dechlorinated feed in many designs. It suits sites where steam is expensive or capacity is limited.
We size both against your daily demand profile and your utility costs, and show you the steam, power and cooling water figures side by side.

pages.headline: Water for Injection by membrane
pages.lead: Our membrane systems produce Water for Injection (WFI) at ambient temperature from double-pass reverse osmosis (RO), electrodeionization (EDI) and ultrafiltration (UF), with no plant steam for generation.

body: USP has long allowed WFI from any process equivalent or superior to distillation. The European Pharmacopoeia did not. In April 2017 the revised Ph. Eur. monograph 0169 began to allow WFI by reverse osmosis, single or double pass, coupled with other suitable techniques such as EDI, ultrafiltration or nanofiltration.

The quality limits did not change. Membrane WFI must meet the same conductivity, TOC and endotoxin limits as distilled WFI. What changed is the evidence inspectors expect: a contamination control strategy, as EU GMP Annex 1 describes, that shows how the system controls microbes and endotoxins without the heat of distillation.

pages.headline: Pretreatment
pages.lead: Pretreatment protects your reverse osmosis (RO) membranes and stills from chlorine, chloramine, hardness and particles, so the purification stage downstream runs to its design life.

blocks.h: Start from the water you have
body: USP requires feed water for pharmaceutical water to meet drinking water standards such as those of the US EPA, and in Canada most sites draw municipal water that meets the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality. Drinking water standards protect people, not membranes.

Many Canadian municipal supplies use chloramine as a secondary disinfectant, and it passes through softeners and attacks polyamide RO membranes. Spring runoff raises turbidity and organic load, and winter supply can fall to 2–5 °C. We design pretreatment from a year of your water data, not one sample.

Activated carbon or sodium bisulfite dosing removes chlorine and chloramine. A 5 µm cartridge filter protects the RO pumps.
